title: RAFT: Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms for Optical Flow

01_initial_request.target_name: RAFT (Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms), an end-to-end trainable deep neural network architecture for dense optical-flow estimation between two RGB video frames
01_initial_request.input_data: Pairs of consecutive RGB images with optical-flow supervision from FlyingChairs, FlyingThings3D, Sintel, KITTI-2015, and HD1K; prior architectural ideas including learned per-pixel features, 4D all-pairs cost/correlation volumes, iterative refinement, convolutional GRUs, and optimization-inspired update rules. The implemented model used 1/8-resolution feature maps with D=256 channels, a 4-layer correlation pyramid with pooling kernel sizes {1, 2, 4, 8}, and recurrent flow updates initialized from zero or from a warm start.
01_initial_request.user_intent: Prior optical-flow systems struggled with fast motion, occlusions, motion blur, textureless regions, poor cross-dataset generalization, expensive multi-stage coarse-to-fine cascades, and difficulty recovering from early coarse-resolution errors. The authors aimed to replace hand-designed objectives and coarse-to-fine learned pipelines with a single-resolution recurrent architecture that could use both small- and large-displacement evidence and train efficiently.
01_initial_request.quantifiable_goal: Achieve state-of-the-art optical-flow accuracy by improving on the best published KITTI-15 test F1-all error of 6.10% and Sintel final-pass test endpoint error of 4.098 pixels, while retaining practical efficiency: fewer training iterations than prior multi-stage networks, low parameter count, and real-time-scale inference on GPU.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] Traditional optical flow was formulated as energy minimization with data and regularization terms, while recent CNN methods such as FlowNet2, PWC-Net, LiteFlowNet, VCN, and MaskFlowNet used learned coarse-to-fine prediction. [Gap] Coarse-to-fine cascades can miss small fast-moving objects, propagate early low-resolution mistakes, require many training iterations, and may generalize poorly to unseen scenes. [Decision] Frame RAFT as an optimization-inspired learned architecture that maintains a single high-resolution flow estimate and refines it recurrently instead of using a fixed coarse-to-fine cascade.
02_agent_trajectory.observation: The authors identified that maintaining and iteratively updating one flow field could preserve fine detail while avoiding the limitations of coarse-to-fine pyramids, and that all-pairs correlation could expose both small and large displacements to every update.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] Learned features are effective descriptors for matching pixels across frames, and DCFlow showed the value of 4D cost volumes over learned features. [Gap] Existing cost-volume processing such as semi-global matching was not fully differentiable end-to-end for direct optical-flow loss optimization. [Decision] Design a differentiable feature encoder and all-pairs correlation layer so that feature extraction and matching can be trained jointly with the final flow objective.

tool.name: RAFT feature encoder and all-pairs correlation volume

parameters.input: two consecutive RGB images I1 and I2
parameters.feature_encoder_architecture: 6 residual blocks: 2 at 1/2 resolution, 2 at 1/4 resolution, 2 at 1/8 resolution
parameters.correlation_volume_shape: H x W x H x W at feature resolution
parameters.correlation_operation: dot product / inner product between all pairs of feature vectors

02_agent_trajectory.observation: The design produced per-pixel feature maps for both images and a dense 4D correlation volume computed efficiently as a matrix multiplication, allowing every pixel in I1 to compare against every pixel in I2.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] Large motions require access to wide spatial context, while small fast-moving objects require high-resolution information. [Gap] A single local cost volume has limited range, but a coarse-to-fine pyramid can lose fine structure and be hard to initialize with past-frame motion. [Decision] Build a multi-scale correlation pyramid by pooling only the last two dimensions of the all-pairs volume, preserving the I1 dimensions at high resolution while giving lower-resolution lookup levels a larger effective displacement range.

tool.name: Correlation pyramid and bilinear correlation lookup

parameters.pooled_dimensions: last two dimensions corresponding to I2 coordinates
parameters.lowest_level_effective_range: 256 pixels at original resolution for k=4 and radius=4
parameters.sampling: bilinear sampling on real-valued lookup grids

02_agent_trajectory.observation: The resulting correlation-pyramid lookup concatenated local neighborhoods from all pyramid levels around the current estimated correspondence, providing both fine and coarse displacement evidence for recurrent updates.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] Iterative optimization methods refine a current solution by repeated updates, and recurrent neural units can share weights across many iterations. [Gap] Prior learned refinement modules often used untied weights, fixed numbers of stages, or large networks, limiting iteration count and efficiency. [Decision] Use a lightweight convolutional-GRU update operator with tied weights that consumes current flow, correlation features, context features from I1, and a hidden state to predict incremental flow updates.

parameters.alternative_initialization: warm-start by forward projecting previous frame-pair flow and filling occlusion gaps by nearest-neighbor interpolation
parameters.update_inputs: current flow, correlation features, flow features, context-network features, hidden state
parameters.weight_tying: same update-operator weights reused across iterations

02_agent_trajectory.observation: The update block generated a sequence of flow estimates from f0=0 and was designed to converge to a fixed flow field. The authors reported that the update operator could be applied for 100+ iterations during inference without divergence.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] RAFT predicts optical flow at 1/8 resolution, but benchmarks evaluate full-resolution endpoint error and KITTI outlier rates. [Gap] Simple bilinear upsampling can blur motion boundaries and lose small moving objects. [Decision] Add a learned convex upsampling module that predicts a mask over a 3x3 neighborhood of coarse flow vectors for each full-resolution pixel.

parameters.mask_shape: H/8 x W/8 x (8 x 8 x 9)

02_agent_trajectory.observation: The learned upsampling module produced full-resolution H x W x 2 flow fields and was reported to improve accuracy particularly near motion boundaries and for small fast-moving objects.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] Supervised optical-flow datasets provide ground-truth flow, and prior work typically pretrains on synthetic data before dataset-specific finetuning. [Gap] The new recurrent architecture needed an end-to-end training schedule that encourages all intermediate predictions to improve while remaining efficient. [Decision] Train RAFT in PyTorch with AdamW, supervised L1 loss over the full sequence of flow predictions with exponentially increasing weights, and staged pretraining/finetuning across synthetic and real benchmarks.

parameters.sequence_loss: L1 distance to ground-truth flow over all predicted flows
parameters.photometric_augmentation: Torchvision ColorJitter brightness 0.4, contrast 0.4, saturation 0.4, hue 0.5/pi; KITTI reduced to 0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.3/pi

02_agent_trajectory.observation: The model was trained from random initialization using staged synthetic pretraining and benchmark finetuning. The reported full RAFT training for C+T used 200k iterations on 2 GPUs in the timing comparison, substantially fewer than many prior networks.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] A key claim was that the architecture should generalize from synthetic training data to unseen benchmark distributions. [Gap] Dataset-specific finetuning can obscure whether the architecture itself generalizes. [Decision] Evaluate RAFT trained only on FlyingChairs plus FlyingThings on Sintel train and KITTI-15 train without dataset-specific finetuning.

parameters.reported_model_selection: 3 random seeds; report model with median Sintel clean-pass train accuracy

02_agent_trajectory.observation: RAFT achieved Sintel train clean EPE 1.43, Sintel train final EPE 2.71, KITTI-15 train F1-EPE 5.04, and KITTI-15 train F1-all 17.4%. The KITTI cross-dataset EPE improved over the prior best deep network trained on the same data from 8.36 to 5.04.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] The final target was leaderboard-level state-of-the-art accuracy after standard finetuning. [Gap] Synthetic-only validation did not establish performance on held-out public test sets. [Decision] Finetune using Sintel/KITTI/HD1K mixtures for Sintel and KITTI-specific finetuning for KITTI, then submit/evaluate two-frame and warm-start RAFT variants on public benchmarks.

tool.name: Sintel test and KITTI-15 test leaderboards

parameters.kitti_finetuning_data: KITTI-2015 for additional 50k iterations using Sintel-finetuned weights

02_agent_trajectory.observation: On Sintel test with S+K+H finetuning, RAFT two-frame achieved clean EPE 1.94 and final EPE 3.18; RAFT warm-start achieved clean EPE 1.61 and final EPE 2.86. On KITTI-15 test, RAFT two-frame achieved F1-all 5.10%, outperforming the prior 6.10% result.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] RAFT combined several design choices: ConvGRU recurrence, weight tying, context features, multi-scale correlation pooling, all-pairs correlation, correlation lookup radius, and learned upsampling. [Gap] The authors needed to determine whether accuracy came from the full combination or from incidental training effects. [Decision] Run ablation experiments trained on FlyingChairs plus FlyingThings to isolate architectural components.

parameters.evaluated_datasets: Sintel train clean/final and KITTI-15 train
parameters.components_tested: update operator, weight tying, context, feature scale, lookup radius, correlation pooling, correlation range, refinement features, upsampling, number of inference updates

02_agent_trajectory.observation: The ConvGRU reference with bilinear upsampling achieved Sintel clean EPE 1.63, Sintel final EPE 2.83, KITTI F1-EPE 5.54, KITTI F1-all 19.8%, and 4.8M parameters. Reported qualitative ablations showed that GRU outperformed plain convolutional updates, tied weights improved accuracy and reduced parameter count, context helped, pooling improved results, all-pairs correlation was best overall, correlation outperformed warping especially on KITTI, and learned upsampling improved motion-boundary accuracy.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] All-pairs correlation scales quadratically in pixels, raising concern for high-resolution video, and recurrent inference could be slow if many updates are required. [Gap] State-of-the-art accuracy alone would not establish practical utility. [Decision] Measure parameter count, inference time, training iterations, and scalability to 1080p DAVIS video.

tool.name: Runtime, parameter-count, and DAVIS high-resolution evaluation

02_agent_trajectory.observation: The full RAFT model had 5.3M parameters, ran in 0.10 s on a GTX 1080Ti for the standard timing setting, used 200k training iterations on 2 GPUs, and achieved Sintel train final EPE 2.83 in the timing table. RAFT-S used 1.0M parameters, ran in 0.05 s, and achieved EPE 3.37. On 1088x1920 DAVIS video, 12 iterations took 550 ms per frame, with all-pairs correlation taking 95 ms. The paper also reported 1088x436 videos at 10 frames/s on a 1080Ti GPU and the smaller model at 20 frames/s.

03_success_verification.validation_technique: Benchmark evaluation on Sintel train/test and KITTI-15 train/test, cross-dataset generalization from FlyingChairs+FlyingThings, controlled ablation studies, and runtime/parameter-count measurements on GTX 1080Ti plus high-resolution DAVIS video.

KITTI_15_test_F1_all.interpretation: RAFT two-frame achieved the best reported KITTI-15 test outlier error, improving over the prior published 6.10% by about 16% relative error reduction.

Sintel_test_final_EPE_warm_start.interpretation: RAFT warm-start achieved state-of-the-art Sintel final-pass test endpoint error, about a 30% relative reduction from the prior 4.098-pixel result.

Sintel_test_clean_EPE_warm_start.interpretation: Warm-start RAFT ranked first on the Sintel clean-pass test set in the reported comparison.

Sintel_test_final_EPE_two_frame.interpretation: The zero-initialized two-frame RAFT model also outperformed prior Sintel final-pass methods after S+K+H finetuning.

cross_dataset_KITTI_15_train_EPE.interpretation: When trained only on FlyingChairs and FlyingThings, RAFT reduced KITTI-15 train EPE from the prior best comparable 8.36 to 5.04, demonstrating strong generalization.

cross_dataset_Sintel_train_clean_EPE.interpretation: With only FlyingChairs+FlyingThings training, RAFT obtained lower Sintel clean train error than prior methods in the reported table.

full_model_parameter_count.interpretation: RAFT achieved state-of-the-art accuracy with far fewer parameters than FlowNet2's 162M parameters and comparable or fewer parameters than several prior optical-flow CNNs.

standard_inference_time_1080Ti.interpretation: Runtime for the full RAFT model after 10 updates on the authors' GTX 1080Ti timing setup.

DAVIS_1080p_runtime.interpretation: Runtime for 12 RAFT iterations on 1088x1920 DAVIS video, showing scalability to high-resolution input.

DAVIS_1080p_all_pairs_correlation_time.interpretation: Time spent computing all-pairs correlation within the 550 ms high-resolution inference run.

03_success_verification.final_verdict: The original goal was met. RAFT surpassed the prior best published KITTI-15 test F1-all error of 6.10% with 5.10%, and surpassed the prior Sintel final-pass test EPE of 4.098 pixels with approximately 2.855 pixels for the warm-start model. It also showed strong synthetic-to-real generalization, lower parameter count than many prior methods, fewer training iterations than large cascade models, and practical GPU inference speed, while ablations supported the importance of the recurrent all-pairs design.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Replacing the convolutional GRU update operator with plain convolutional layers degraded performance.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: The authors attributed the GRU advantage to gated activation, which made it easier for the sequence of flow estimates to converge.
04_failure_modes.correction: Use the ConvGRU-based update operator in the final RAFT model.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Using separate untied weights for each update operator did not improve the model and increased parameter count.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: Untied update blocks weakened the optimization-like recurrent structure and made the model less parameter-efficient.
04_failure_modes.correction: Tie the update-operator weights across all recurrent iterations.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Removing the context network reduced accuracy, although the model still remained competitive.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: Directly injecting first-image context features into the update operator helps aggregate spatial information within motion boundaries.
04_failure_modes.correction: Retain the context encoder features as inputs to the update operator.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Removing multi-scale correlation pooling worsened results.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: Without pooling, the lookup features did not capture large and small displacements as effectively.
04_failure_modes.correction: Keep the 4-level pooled correlation pyramid with pooling kernel sizes 1, 2, 4, and 8.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Restricting the correlation volume to local neighborhoods of 32, 64, or 128 pixels was not best overall.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: A fixed local range can miss larger displacements and requires selecting a range hyperparameter; all-pairs correlation avoids this limitation and is convenient to compute by matrix multiplication.
04_failure_modes.correction: Use all-pairs correlation in the final model.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Replacing correlation-volume lookup with feature warping was less accurate, especially on KITTI.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: Warping features using the current flow estimate provides less rich matching information than querying the all-pairs correlation volume.
04_failure_modes.correction: Use correlation features for recurrent refinement instead of a warping-only refinement module.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Bilinear upsampling produced worse results than the learned upsampling module.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: Bilinear interpolation blurs motion boundaries and is less able to recover small fast-moving objects.
04_failure_modes.correction: Use the learned convex 3x3-neighborhood upsampling mask in the final high-resolution flow prediction.
